description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:164

```rust
pub fn new_with_accounts(account_ids: &[&str]) -> Self {
    let b = Self::new();
    {
        let mut inner = b.inner.lock().unwrap();
        for id in account_ids {
            inner.known_accounts.insert((*id).to_owned());
        }
    }
    b
}
```

This is a cookie-cutter divergence from the canonical extension-server
template. Confirmed by grepping all six extension-server siblings:

| Crate | Add-known-account API |
|---|---|
| jmap-mail-server (canonical) | `register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)` |
| jmap-chat-server | `register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)` |
| jmap-calendars-server | `register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)` |
| jmap-contacts-server | `register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)` |
| jmap-tasks-server | `register_account(&self, account_id: &Id)` |
| **jmap-sharing-server** | `new_with_accounts(account_ids: &[&str]) -> Self` (divergent) |
| jmap-filenode-server | `with_account(self, &str) -> Self` (also divergent) |

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" rule: if you reshape a
sibling in a way that diverges from `jmap-mail-server`, change
`jmap-mail-server` first then propagate. This crate diverged without
that. The propagation choice is reversible (either bring sharing-server
in line with `register_account(&self, &Id)`, or change the canonical
to a `new_with_accounts` pattern and propagate).

API-contract specifics of the divergent shape:

1. Constructor-only access. Callers that need to register an account
   *after* MemoryBackend construction (the common test pattern of
   "construct, exercise some methods that populate one account, then
   add a second account") cannot. The canonical `&self`-receiver shape
   supports this naturally.

2. `&[&str]` is the most restrictive str slice shape. Callers with
   `Vec<String>` must write
   `&accs.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>()` boilerplate
   every time. `impl IntoIterator<Item = impl AsRef<str>>` is the
   idiomatic alternative. The canonical `&Id` shape sidesteps this
   by accepting an owned-or-borrowed Id newtype.

3. The constructor-shape signature is locked. A future
   `register_account(&self, ...)` addition is non-breaking, but the
   workspace already has a 6-sibling convention that callers will
   reach for first. Documenting the divergence is one option; the
   cleaner option is to add `register_account` and either deprecate
   or document `new_with_accounts` as a convenience.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream user
of multiple extension-server crates (e.g. someone wiring the testjig)
writes ergonomic test setup against `register_account` for five
crates and runs into a different idiom for sharing-server. Bug
reports of the form "why does sharing-server work differently" are
the predictable cost.
notes: Added register_account(&self, &Id) matching the canonical jmap-mail-server shape. Reshaped new_with_accounts to delegate to register_account so the two APIs share the underlying register-by-Id path. new_with_accounts is retained as an ergonomic constructor (with rustdoc explaining the canonical alignment and preferred-for-new-code status of register_account).
title: MemoryBackend::new_with_accounts(&[&str]) diverges from canonical register_account(&self, &Id) — locks awkward constructor shape
